_comment: Live sandbox Control runtime gates. This file is the source of truth for
the seven Authority/Hub runtime opt-ins that used to exist only as
workflow_dispatch inputs typed from operator memory.
Why it exists: every gate's committed Terraform default is the dark value
(false / null) because the foundation was built dark-first. Live sandbox is
the opposite on all seven. Any unattended plan that fell back to those
defaults would not deploy the Hub, it would destroy it -- returning the
gates to their committed-closed defaults IS the documented rollback (see
docs/runbooks/prod-rollout-ledger/2026-08-06-unlock-prod-control-root.md).
So the automatic deploy leg in build-and-push.yml reads its gates from
here, and control-sandbox-update.yml asserts its dispatch inputs match,
which keeps the attended and unattended paths from diverging.
terraform-plan-pr.yml reads them too, so editing this file is itself a
plan input: the PR that changes a gate plans the change it proposes.
Changing a value here changes live sandbox on the next main push. Treat it
as the rollout step it is: land it with the reviewed plan that carries the
matching Terraform, not ahead of it.
One exception: turning ALL seven dark is a teardown of the Hub and the
Authority runtime, not a deploy. The automatic leg fails closed on that
shape rather than applying it, so a full rollback stays attended --
dispatch control-sandbox-update.yml and read the destroy plan first. A
partial rollback (some gates dark) does auto-apply. The PR lane is the
deliberate exception to that fail-closed rule: it only plans, so it
renders the all-dark destroy plan instead of refusing it.
Values below were bound to the 2026-08-07 apply (run 31181195766, commit

3a44c954) and confirmed against live AWS -- EXCEPT the two proof colours, which are the target of the catch-up cutover rather than a live reading. They diverge from live until that applies, which is the point: editing this file IS the rollout step.
